posts.title: Pre-Fezgiving Treat
posts.description: It’s been a bit of a slow period since our last update in early August. We’ve only acquired four new fezzes for the collection since then. But, we figured a Fezgiving treat was due, so we wanted to provide a quick update on our acquisitions. Our first update is a double feature, over in the Religious Groups exhibit, in the Nuwabian section. We have added a white fez, similar in design to the others we previously acquired. However, the big news is a new black Nuwabian fez, full of rhinestones and mystery. Check it out! The Clandestine Masonry exhibit received an update with a new International Masons fez. This one is distinct in that it is maroon, with a long yellow tassel. Most unlike our other International Mason fezzes! But, we saved the best for last. Check out our latest, brand new exhibit, on the Ancient and Heroic Order of the Gordian Knot . This small, side degree of Freemasonry has a fun bit of history and worthwhile goal. Enjoy your holiday season, everyone!

posts.title: Muggy Fezzy Updates
posts.description: I’m about a month ahead of schedule this year. I usually spend Labor Day weekend updating the Museum, but apparently I got ambitious. The Clandestine Masons page has two new International Masons fezzes, including a particularly flashy rhinestone example and an Order of the Eastern Star fez from Syracuse, New York. The United Ancient Order of Druids section received a rare red “Past Arch” fez that you’ll want to check out. We added another Bassora fez to the Princes of Bagdad collection. As always, when Princes of Bagdad material appears, we tend to buy it. There are also a new piece in the Grand United Order of Odd Fellows section, from the mysterious Past Grand Master’s Council No. 16… at least, we think. Finally, the biggest update is to the Caliphs of Bagdad page. A fez and 1929 flyer acquired from friend of the Museum Matt Cordoves finally gave us enough information to substantially expand the history of this wonderfully obscure New Castle, Pennsylvania, organization. posts.title: Sweet Fezzy Memories
posts.description: It is Memorial Day in the United States. After tending to several fraternal plots in our local town, we took a moment to add five new finds for our fez enthusiasts. First, we have a new Odd Fellows lodge fez added to the IOOF exhibit. Next is a new AMOS fez from the interregnum “volcano emblem” period, now on display in the Odd Fellows Social Bodies area. The Shriners exhibit has also been updated with a very small Abou Saad Shrine fez. A rare addition to the collection is a Women of Woodcraft fez, now featured in the Woodmen of the World section. Last but not least is a previously difficult-to-identify fez from the Junior Order of American Mechanics’ affiliated side degree, the Order of the Orient. Thank you for checking back, and have a great summer.
